name: Anyword
subcategory: AI drafting, research and content optimization
tagline: Draft and compare marketing variants against a defined audience and brand voice

pricing.notes: Official self-serve starter amount; annual terms may be emphasized.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1 seat; 1 workspace; monthly billing includes 50 predictions/month and 50 data rows; annual card lists 100 predictions/month.

tiers.name: Data-Driven
tiers.limits: 3 seats; 5 workspaces; monthly billing includes 100 predictions/month, annual card lists 175; 50 data rows.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 7-day trial, numeric trial allowance not separately published
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for self-serve plans; Business and Enterprise are quote-based
pricing.hiddenCosts: Data-Driven extra seats cost $59/month or $49/month on annual billing, with a published maximum of 10 seats.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Anyword, draft and compare marketing variants against a defined audience and brand voice. The hard boundary is predictive performance data, brand governance, and campaign integrations, plus workflow, data, and model tuning.
coreLoopDIY: Take a brief with a defined audience and brand voice, gather user-supplied source material, generate and compare structured draft variants, and keep citations and revisions attached to each section.
whatYouLose: predictive performance data, brand governance, and campaign integrations
ongoingBurden: prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Anyword because the subscription bundles a refined workflow, proprietary signals, templates, and predictable output quality for a team. The recurring cost buys prompt maintenance, retrieval quality, source handling, provider changes, and editorial QA, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Open WebUI
priorArt.desc: Active open-source interface for local and API-backed language models with retrieval features.

alternatives.name: AnythingLLM
alternatives.desc: A local-first AI workspace with saved agents, files, memory, and reusable context; the model is yours, so the brand voice can be too.

facts.install: Desktop installer for macOS/Windows/Linux, or Docker for a self-hosted web instance
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp models plus Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI and many cloud APIs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, OpenRouter and Mistral
facts.dataFormat: Desktop data stays in the app's local storage; self-hosted data is stored in the mounted server storage and chosen vector database (LanceDB by default), while prompts sent to cloud models leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can preserve brand context and generate variants, but it has no Anyword-style predictive performance scoring or audience-trained marketing analytics.
facts.setupBlocker: The installer is easy, but useful results still require downloading a local model or supplying a model-provider API key

alternatives.name: Jan
alternatives.desc: A desktop ChatGPT-shaped box with local models and reusable assistants; excellent at prompts, blissfully unaware of your marketing calendar.

facts.install: Download the macOS, Windows or Linux desktop installer
facts.engines: Built-in local inference via llama.cpp/llama-server plus OpenAI-compatible APIs and connectors such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter
facts.dataFormat: Threads, assistants, settings and downloaded model files live in Jan's local data folder; only requests sent to configured cloud providers leave the machine
facts.gapVsPaid: It can follow a saved brand prompt, but it lacks Anyword's structured campaign templates, audience controls, and predictive copy scores.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use requires downloading a multi-gigabyte model and enough RAM; cloud use requires an API key

alternatives.name: Open WebUI
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted AI workbench with saved prompts, knowledge, web search, and multi-model comparison; powerful, not especially house-trained.

facts.install: Run the official Docker image, install the Python package, or deploy with Kubernetes
facts.engines: Ollama and any OpenAI-compatible API, including LM Studio, vLLM, Groq, Mistral and OpenRouter; additional speech, image and search providers
facts.dataFormat: By default, chats and account data live in a local SQLite webui.db, uploads in a data/uploads directory and embeddings in the configured vector store; PostgreSQL and object storage are optional
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a capable general workbench, not a marketing optimization product with audience profiles, performance predictions, and variant analytics.
facts.setupBlocker: A non-expert must install Docker or a compatible Python environment, mount persistent storage correctly, and separately provide Ollama or an API endpoint

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a personal content workstation DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Anyword in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and the OpenAI Responses API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: take a brief with a defined audience and brand voice, gather user-supplied source material, generate and compare structured draft variants, and keep citations and revisions attached to each section.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Build a brief form with audience, objective, tone, source URLs, and prohibited claims.
Store imported source text locally and chunk it for retrieval with SQLite FTS5.
Generate an outline first and require approval before drafting sections.
Attach source references to generated paragraphs and flag unsupported claims.
Provide rewrite controls for shorten, clarify, change tone, and add evidence.
Export clean Markdown plus a JSON research bundle.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out live search-engine rank data.
Deliberately leave out automatic publishing to third-party CMSs.
Deliberately leave out multi-user approvals and brand governance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
